direct_answer: Vopak integrates sustainability-related performance into remuneration/incentive schemes by translating targets from its strategic framework and sustainability roadmap into remuneration incentives linked to key sustainability performance areas, specifically: Total Injury Rate (TIR), Process Safety Event Rate (PSER), gender diversity, and GHG emissions reduction [Source 1]. Vopak also states it has implemented board-level remuneration policies aligned with its GHG reduction goals, and that the GHG emissions reduction metric is part of the Executive Board’s (EB) short- and long-term incentive program [Source 4].
compliance_rationale: The evidence confirms that sustainability targets (TIR, PSER, gender diversity, GHG emissions reduction) are linked to remuneration incentives and that GHG reduction is included in the EB’s short- and long-term incentive program [Source 1][Source 4]. However, the retrieved passages do not provide the key characteristics of the incentive schemes, the proportion of variable remuneration tied to sustainability metrics, nor the approval/update level for the scheme terms, and they do not explicitly cover supervisory body remuneration integration beyond a general reference to “board-level” policies [Source 4].
disclosure_gaps: Key characteristics/design of the incentive schemes (e.g., STI/LTI structure details, weighting approach, measurement periods) beyond stating that certain targets are linked to remuneration [Source 1][Source 4].

Whether performance is assessed against specific quantified sustainability targets/thresholds (e.g., target values for TIR/PSER, gender diversity, GHG reduction) and how achievement is determined [Source 1][Source 4].
How sustainability-related metrics are used as performance benchmarks within remuneration policies (calculation method, scorecards, gateways, malus/clawback links) [Source 1][Source 4].
Proportion/percentage of variable remuneration dependent on sustainability-related targets/impacts (required by ESRS 2 GOV-3(d))—not provided in retrieved passages.
Governance level at which incentive scheme terms are approved and updated (required by ESRS 2 GOV-3(e))—not provided in retrieved passages.

Explicit coverage for members of the supervisory body (SB) and administrative body (if applicable): the passages mention EB incentives and “board-level remuneration policies” but do not specify SB remuneration linkage to sustainability metrics [Source 4].
key_findings: Sustainability targets from Vopak’s strategic framework and sustainability roadmap are translated into remuneration incentives linked to TIR, PSER, gender diversity, and GHG emissions reduction [Source 1].
Vopak has board-level remuneration policies aligned with GHG reduction goals [Source 4].
The GHG emissions reduction metric is part of the Executive Board’s short- and long-term incentive program [Source 4].
